source: AI Agent Orchestration 2026 Enterprise Playbook (FifthRow / RankSquire synthesis)
summary: Industry synthesis of the 2026 enterprise agent orchestration landscape: convergence on single-orchestrator-with-ephemeral-subagents pattern across Anthropic, OpenAI, AutoGen, and LangChain; A2A protocol joining MCP under AAIF.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge already implements the dominant pattern (single orchestrator, CLI subagents, deterministic state machine). No new capability gap identified.

source: Karpathy LLM Wiki Pattern (GitHub Gist + blog coverage)
summary: Karpathy's April 2026 pattern: an LLM agent compiles raw materials into a persistent, interlinked Markdown wiki; subsequent queries target the wiki instead of raw documents, compounding knowledge with each ingest.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — AgentForge already ships skill distillation (distillationAgent.ts, agentSkillRepository.ts). A wiki-style persistent knowledge store would extend that, but HID-188 (cross-run episodic memory) tracks the adjacent gap. Backlog ≥10 prevents issue creation.

source: A2A (Agent-to-Agent) Protocol under AAIF / Linux Foundation
summary: Agent2Agent protocol (A2A) joined MCP under Linux Foundation AAIF in Dec 2025, standardizing how agents negotiate, delegate, and share context across organizational boundaries.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge is a single-orchestrator system; there is no agent-to-agent communication surface. Adopting A2A would require significant architecture change and has no verified gap to close.

source: ZenBrain: A Neuroscience-Inspired 7-Layer Memory Architecture for Autonomous AI Systems
summary: Open-source 7-layer memory (working, short-term, episodic, long-term, procedural, core, predictive) with 15 neuroscience mechanisms: FSRS scheduling, Hebbian learning, neuromodulator dynamics, TripleCopyMemory. Beats Letta/Mem0/A-Mem on LoCoMo benchmark.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — directly relevant to run-outcome episodic memory gap, but HID-188 already tracks this theme. Backlog cap (11 open issues ≥10) prevents issue creation this run. Worth revisiting after HID-188 ships to see if the decay/FSRS scheduling adds value.

source: Skill-SD: Skill-Conditioned Self-Distillation for Multi-turn LLM Agents
summary: Framework that summarizes completed agent trajectories into compact natural-language skills; teacher branch during training sees retrieved skills while student operates on ordinary context. Achieves +14% on AppWorld, +10.9% on Sokoban over vanilla GRPO.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — very closely adjacent to AgentForge's shipped skill distillation pipeline (distillationAgent.ts + agentSkillRepository.ts). The gap it addresses (executor prompts don't receive skills) is the unshipped part of HID-188. No new Linear issue needed; HID-188 covers it.

source: AgentFugue: Agent Scaling for Long-Horizon Tasks through Collective Reasoning
summary: Collective reasoning framework where peer agents share a reasoning hub that records concise notes on what each has established or ruled out; trained with SFT + end-to-end RL. Improves over strong baselines on long-horizon tasks without centralized planning.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — requires parallel agent execution which AgentForge explicitly deferred (sequential determinism is a design choice). Collective reasoning hub adds infrastructure not in roadmap.

source: Always-On Agents: A Survey of Persistent Memory, State, and Governance in LLM Agents
summary: 435-work survey defining always-on agents through six diagnostic axes (authority, scope, mutability, provenance, recoverability, actionability) and a full state lifecycle. Finds that the literature concentrates on accumulating/retrieving state rather than governing or recovering it.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — strong reference for HID-188 (episodic memory). The governance/recoverability framing surfaces no AgentForge-specific gap beyond what HID-188 already captures. Useful background reading for the implementer of HID-188.

source: LangGraph v1.0 GA (enterprise multi-agent framework by LangChain)
summary: LangGraph reached v1.0 in late 2025; surpassed CrewAI in GitHub stars in early 2026. Graph-based architecture maps to audit trails and rollback points. Largest production deployment footprint in 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge is a custom state machine orchestrator, not built on LangGraph. No new adoptable pattern identified beyond what AgentForge already implements (explicit state machine, artifact model).

summary: Microsoft promoted AutoGen v2 event-driven architecture to general availability in February 2026. Features multi-agent debate and verification patterns. Strong in research/academic settings.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses a sequential deterministic state machine by design. AutoGen's event-driven multi-agent patterns require architectural changes that have been deliberately deferred.

source: DeerFlow v2 by ByteDance (GitHub trending July 2026)
summary: Open-source super agent harness (ByteDance) that orchestrates sub-agents, memory, sandboxes, and extensible skills. Hit #1 on GitHub Trending after v2.0 launch in July 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — covers similar territory to AgentForge (agent orchestration + memory + skills) but is a competing framework, not an adoptable pattern. No actionable gap identified.

source: MAGMA: Multi-Graph based Agentic Memory Architecture
summary: Stores episodic events in a dedicated event subgraph with cross-graph traversal for multi-hop temporal queries. Achieved highest LoCoMo judge score of 0.7 as of early 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — directly relevant to episodic memory, but HID-188 already tracks the cross-run episodic memory gap for AgentForge. Graph-based storage would be new infrastructure beyond HID-188's scope.
